get_user_info.title: Get the current user
get_user_info.description: Read the user id behind the personal access token, plus the scopes the token holds and, with user.email:read, the email address. The cheapest call that proves the token works.

output.description: The token's user id, scopes and (if permitted) email.

list_bases.title: List bases
list_bases.description: List the bases the token can access, with each base's id, name and permission level. Results are paged 1,000 at a time; pass the returned offset to continue. Use get_base_schema to see a base's tables and fields.

offset.description: Cursor from the previous response's offset.

output.description: A page of bases, with an offset when more remain.

bases.description: Each with id, name and permissionLevel.

get_base_schema.title: Get a base's schema
get_base_schema.description: Read every table in a base with its id, name, primary field, fields (id, name, type, options) and views. Call this before reading or writing records to learn the exact field names and types.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

output.description: The base's tables, each with fields and views.

tables.description: Each with id, name, primaryFieldId, fields and views.

create_base.title: Create a base
create_base.description: Create a new base in a workspace with one or more tables. Each table needs a name and at least one field; the first field becomes the primary field. Returns the new base id and its table schema.

workspace_id.description: Workspace to create the base in (starts with wsp).

tables.description: Tables to create, each {name, description?, fields: [{name, type, options?}]}.

output.description: The created base's id and tables.

create_table.title: Create a table
create_table.description: Add a table to a base. Provide a name and its fields; the first field is the primary field and must be a supported primary type such as singleLineText. Use create_field to add fields later.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

fields.description: Fields to create, each {name, type, description?, options?}.

description.description: Description of the table (up to 20,000 characters).

output.description: The created table with its fields and views.

update_table.title: Update a table
update_table.description: Rename a table or change its description. Field changes go through create_field and update_field.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

create_field.title: Create a field
create_field.description: Add a field (column) to a table. `type` is an Airtable field type such as singleLineText, number, singleSelect, multipleRecordLinks or date; most types need `options` (e.g. {precision: 0} for number, {choices: [...]} for selects).

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

type.description: Airtable field type, e.g. singleLineText, number, singleSelect, checkbox, date.

options.description: Type-specific options, e.g. {choices: [{name: 'Todo'}]} for a select.

update_field.title: Update a field
update_field.description: Rename a field or change its description. A field's type and options cannot be changed through the API.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

list_records.title: List records in a table
list_records.description: Page through a table's records, up to 100 per page. Narrow with filter_by_formula (an Airtable formula such as {Status} = 'Done'), limit columns with fields, order with sort, or apply a view's filters and order with view. Pass the returned offset to get the next page.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

max_records.description: Stop after this many records in total.

offset.description: Cursor from the previous response's offset.

view.description: View id or name; applies that view's filters and order.

filter_by_formula.description: Airtable formula deciding which records come back.

fields.description: Only return these fields, by name or id.

cell_format.description: json (default) for typed values, or string for display strings (then time_zone and user_locale are required).

time_zone.description: IANA time zone used when cell_format is string, e.g. America/New_York.

user_locale.description: Locale used when cell_format is string, e.g. en-gb.

return_fields_by_field_id.description: Key the returned fields by field id instead of field name.

record_metadata.description: Extra per-record metadata to include; commentCount is the supported value.

output.description: A page of records, with an offset when more remain.

records.description: Each with id, createdTime and fields.

offset.description: Pass back to fetch the next page.

get_record.title: Get a record
get_record.description: Fetch one record by id with all of its non-empty fields. Empty fields are omitted from the response.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

return_fields_by_field_id.description: Key the returned fields by field id instead of field name.

fields.description: Cell values keyed by field name (or id).

create_records.title: Create records
create_records.description: Create up to 10 records in one call. Each item is {"fields": {...}} keyed by field name or id. Set typecast to let Airtable coerce strings and create missing select options.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

typecast.description: Let Airtable convert string values to the field's type, e.g. create missing select options.

return_fields_by_field_id.description: Key the returned fields by field id instead of field name.

records.description: The new records with their ids.

update_records.title: Update records
update_records.description: Change fields on up to 10 existing records. Each item is {"id": "rec...", "fields": {...}}; only the fields named are written and the rest are left as they are. Use replace_records to clear unnamed fields, or upsert_records to match on a field instead of an id.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

typecast.description: Let Airtable convert string values to the field's type, e.g. create missing select options.

return_fields_by_field_id.description: Key the returned fields by field id instead of field name.

upsert_records.title: Upsert records
upsert_records.description: Create or update up to 10 records by matching on one to three fields instead of record ids. A record whose merge_on values match an existing row updates it; otherwise a new row is created. The response lists which ids were created and which updated.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

records.description: Up to 10 records, each {"fields": {...}} including the merge_on fields.

merge_on.description: One to three field names or ids that identify a record.

typecast.description: Let Airtable convert string values to the field's type, e.g. create missing select options.

output.description: The affected records, with createdRecords and updatedRecords id lists.

replace_records.title: Replace records
replace_records.description: Overwrite up to 10 existing records. Unlike update_records, any field you do not include is cleared. Each item is {"id": "rec...", "fields": {...}}.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

typecast.description: Let Airtable convert string values to the field's type, e.g. create missing select options.

update_record.title: Update a record
update_record.description: Change fields on one record; fields you do not name are left untouched. Use update_records for several records at once.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

fields.description: Field values to write, keyed by field name or id.

typecast.description: Let Airtable convert string values to the field's type, e.g. create missing select options.

fields.description: Cell values keyed by field name (or id).

delete_record.title: Delete a record
delete_record.description: Permanently delete one record by id. Deleted records can only be recovered from the base's trash in the Airtable UI for a limited time.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

output.description: The deleted record's id and a deleted flag.

list_comments.title: List a record's comments
list_comments.description: List the comments on a record, newest first, with each comment's author, text, mentions and reactions. Page with the returned offset.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

offset.description: Cursor from the previous response's offset.

comments.description: Each with id, author, text, createdTime.

create_comment.title: Comment on a record
create_comment.description: Add a comment to a record as the token's user. Mention a user with @[usrXXXXXXXXXXXXXX] in the text. Set parent_comment_id to reply in a thread.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

parent_comment_id.description: Id of the comment to reply to.

update_comment.title: Edit a comment
update_comment.description: Change the text of a comment. Only the comment's own author can edit it.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

delete_comment.title: Delete a comment
delete_comment.description: Delete a comment from a record. Non-admin users can only delete their own comments.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

output.description: The deleted comment's id and a deleted flag.

upload_attachment.title: Upload an attachment
upload_attachment.description: Upload a file of up to 5 MB straight into an attachment field of an existing record, appended to the attachments already there. The file is sent base64-encoded. For larger files, write a public URL into the field with update_record instead.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

content_type.description: MIME type of the file, e.g. image/png.

filename.description: File name to store, e.g. report.pdf.

output.description: The record id, createdTime and the field's attachments.

sync_csv.title: Sync CSV data into a table
sync_csv.description: Push CSV text (up to 10,000 rows, 2 MB) into a Sync API table. Rows are matched on the primary key column configured when the sync was set up in Airtable; the sync source must already exist.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

table.description: Table id (tbl...) or table name. Ids survive renames.

sync_id.description: The API endpoint sync id shown in the sync's setup.

csv.description: The CSV text, with a header row.

list_webhooks.title: List webhooks
list_webhooks.description: List the webhooks registered on a base with their notification URL, specification, expiry time and whether notifications are enabled.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

webhooks.description: Each with id, notificationUrl, specification, expirationTime.

create_webhook.title: Create a webhook
create_webhook.description: Register a webhook on a base. `specification` says what to watch, e.g. {options: {filters: {dataTypes: ['tableData'], recordChangeScope: 'tbl...'}}}. Airtable pings notification_url when changes happen; fetch the changes with list_webhook_payloads. Webhooks expire after 7 days unless refreshed. The MAC secret is returned only once.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

specification.description: What the webhook watches: {options: {filters: {dataTypes, recordChangeScope?, ...}, includes?}}.

notification_url.description: HTTPS URL to ping on changes. Omit to poll payloads instead.

output.description: The webhook id, its macSecretBase64 and expirationTime.

delete_webhook.title: Delete a webhook
delete_webhook.description: Delete a webhook from a base. Notifications stop and its stored payloads are no longer retrievable.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

list_webhook_payloads.title: List webhook payloads
list_webhook_payloads.description: Read the change payloads a webhook has recorded, oldest first, starting at `cursor`. Keep calling with the returned cursor while mightHaveMore is true. Reading payloads also extends the webhook's life.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

cursor.description: Position to read from; use the cursor from the last response. Starts at 1.

output.description: A batch of payloads with the next cursor.

refresh_webhook.title: Refresh a webhook
refresh_webhook.description: Extend a webhook's expiry by 7 days from now. Webhooks created with a personal access token expire unless refreshed.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

enable_webhook_notifications.title: Enable or disable webhook notifications
enable_webhook_notifications.description: Turn a webhook's notification pings on or off without deleting it. Payloads keep accumulating while pings are off.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

enable.description: true to send notification pings, false to pause them.

list_views.title: List a base's views
list_views.description: List every view in a base with its id, name and type. Available on Business and Enterprise Scale plans.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

include.description: Extra data to include; visibleFieldIds is the supported value.

get_view.title: Get a view
get_view.description: Read one view's metadata: id, name, type and, when asked, the ids of its visible fields. Available on Business and Enterprise Scale plans.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

include.description: Extra data to include; visibleFieldIds is the supported value.

delete_view.title: Delete a view
delete_view.description: Delete a view from a base. The records themselves are untouched. Available on Business and Enterprise Scale plans.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

output.description: The deleted view's id and a deleted flag.

get_base_collaborators.title: Get a base's collaborators
get_base_collaborators.description: Read a base's metadata and who can access it: individual and group collaborators with permission levels and, when asked, pending invite links and interfaces. Enterprise plans only.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

add_base_collaborator.title: Add a base collaborator
add_base_collaborator.description: Give a user or user group access to a base at a permission level. Enterprise plans only.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

collaborators.description: One collaborator: {user: {id}} or {group: {id}} plus permissionLevel (read, comment, edit, create).

update_base_collaborator.title: Change a base collaborator's permission
update_base_collaborator.description: Change the permission level a user or group has on a base. Enterprise plans only.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

remove_base_collaborator.title: Remove a base collaborator
remove_base_collaborator.description: Remove a user's or group's direct access to a base. Access inherited from the workspace is unaffected. Enterprise plans only.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

list_base_shares.title: List a base's shares
list_base_shares.description: List the share links of a base (base, view and form shares) with their state, type and who created them. Enterprise plans only.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

delete_base_share.title: Delete a base share
delete_base_share.description: Permanently delete a share link; anyone using it loses access immediately. Enterprise plans only.

base_id.description: The base id (starts with app), from list_bases.

get_workspace_collaborators.title: Get a workspace's collaborators
get_workspace_collaborators.description: Read a workspace's name, its base ids and who can access it, optionally with collaborators and invite links. Enterprise plans only.

get_enterprise.title: Get an enterprise account
get_enterprise.description: Read an enterprise account's basic information: its workspace ids, user ids, group ids and email domains. Enterprise admins only.

enterprise_account_id.description: The enterprise account id (starts with ent).

get_enterprise_user.title: Get an enterprise user
get_enterprise_user.description: Read one user of an enterprise account: name, email, state, last activity and, when asked, the workspaces, bases and groups they collaborate on. Enterprise admins only.

enterprise_account_id.description: The enterprise account id (starts with ent).

get_user_group.title: Get a user group
get_user_group.description: Read a user group: its name, members and, when asked, the workspaces, bases and interfaces it has access to. Enterprise plans only.

list_audit_log_events.title: List audit log events
list_audit_log_events.description: Page through an enterprise account's audit log, newest first by default. Filter by time window, originating user, event type or affected model id. Enterprise admins only.

enterprise_account_id.description: The enterprise account id (starts with ent).

start_time.description: Only events at or after this ISO 8601 time.

end_time.description: Only events at or before this ISO 8601 time.

originating_user_id.description: Only events performed by this user id.

event_type.description: Only events of this type, e.g. createBase.

model_id.description: Only events affecting this model id (base, table, record...).

next.description: Cursor from the previous response's pagination.next.

previous.description: Cursor from the previous response's pagination.previous.

output.description: A page of audit events with pagination cursors.

events.description: Audit events with actor, action, model and timestamp.
